*[Bug 19091] as.numeric on macOS aarch64 rounds "0.9999999999999999" to 1.0 instead of the nearest IEEE 754 double*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19091>

--- Comment #9 from Suharto Anggono (<mailto:suharto_anggono@yahoo.com|suharto_anggono@yahoo.com>) ---
Works here: approximate the result by a power of 2 and then calculate the
error.

A power of 2 is exactly representable and multiplication by a power of 2 is
exact.

999999999999999*10 is exact.

R> r <- 1
R> sprintf("%a", r + ((999999999999999*10 - r*1e16) + 9)/1e16)
[1] "0x1.fffffffffffffp-1"

For division by 10^22:

R> r <- 2^-20
R> print(r + ((999999999999999*10 - r*1e22) + 9)/1e22, 17)
[1] 9.9999999999999995e-07

It is different from

R> print(999999999999999/1e21 + 9/1e22, 17)
[1] 9.9999999999999974e-07


Otherwise, if not using system 'sccanf' or 'strtod', R could adopt a proven
correct code that doesn't use long double, like David M. Gay's 'strtod' or the
more recent Eisel-Lemire algorithm. Eisel-Lemire algorithm has a C port and
doesn't need big integer for inputs up to 19 digits.

*[Bug 19123] New: Memory leak in `scan()` when a field fails type conversion*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19123>

            Bug ID: 19123
           Summary: Memory leak in `scan()` when a field fails type
                    conversion
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Linux
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3773
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3773&action=edit>
Candidate patch.

## Summary

`scan()` leaks its internal line buffer (an 8 KB `R_StringBuffer`) every
time it aborts on a malformed field. `scanVector()` and `scanFrame()`
allocate the buffer with `R_AllocStringBuffer()` and free it with
`R_FreeStringBuffer()` only on their normal return paths. When a value
cannot be converted to the requested type, `extractItem()` calls
`error()`, which `longjmp`s out of the function and skips the free, so
the buffer is leaked.

Because `read.table()` / `read.csv()` are built on `scan()`, this is
reachable from ordinary data-reading code: every failed parse of an
untrusted or malformed input leaks ~8 KB. A long-running process that
repeatedly reads malformed input accumulates these leaks.

Severity: low. It is a memory leak, not a memory-safety error — no crash
or corruption. The practical impact is unbounded memory growth in a
persistent process that keeps parsing malformed input.

## Affected code

`src/main/scan.c`, `scanVector()` (as of r89873). The buffer is
allocated once, up front:

```
static SEXP scanVector(SEXPTYPE type, R_xlen_t maxitems, R_xlen_t maxlines,
                       int flush, SEXP stripwhite, int blskip, LocalData *d)
{
    ...
    R_StringBuffer strBuf = {NULL, 0, MAXELTSIZE};
    ...
    R_AllocStringBuffer(0, &strBuf);              /* line 571: malloc */
    PROTECT(ans = allocVector(type, blocksize));
    ...
    for (;;) {
        ...
        buffer = fillBuffer(type, strip, &bch, d, &strBuf);
        ...
        extractItem(buffer, ans, n, d);           /* line 617: may error() */
        ...
    }
    ...
    R_FreeStringBuffer(&strBuf);                   /* lines 638/643/674 */
    return bns;
}
```

`extractItem()` throws on a type mismatch via `expected()`:

```
NORET static R_INLINE void expected(char *what, char *got, LocalData *d)
{
    ...
    error(_("scan() expected '%s', got '%s'"), what, got);   /* line 494 */
}
```

The `error()` at line 494 `longjmp`s straight past the
`R_FreeStringBuffer(&strBuf)` calls at lines 638, 643 and 674, so the
`malloc`ed buffer from line 571 is never released. `PROTECT(ans)` is
unwound by the error machinery, but the raw `malloc` in the
`R_StringBuffer` is not.

`scanFrame()` (used for `what = list(...)`, i.e. `read.table()`) has the
same structure: `R_AllocStringBuffer(0, &buf)` at line 699,
`extractItem()` at lines 743/784/806, `R_FreeStringBuffer(&buf)` at line
847 — and leaks identically on error.

## Reproducer

Under an R build configured with `--enable-strict-barrier` and compiled
with `-fsanitize=address` (or run under `valgrind --leak-check=full`):

```
# scanVector path (atomic 'what'):
scan(text = "x", what = 0, quiet = TRUE)
## Error in scan(...) : scan() expected 'a real', got 'x'
##  -> leaks one 8192-byte R_StringBuffer

# scanFrame path (list 'what'; also what read.table uses):
scan(text = "x", what = list(0), quiet = TRUE)

# reachable from read.table()/read.csv() when a column is typed numeric.
# (With the default colClasses the fields are read as character, so there
# is no conversion error and no leak; forcing a numeric column triggers it.)
read.csv(text = "value\nx", colClasses = "numeric")
```

text:
Each failed call leaks 8192 bytes. Repeating it grows RSS without bound.

## Sanitizer output

```
==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks

Direct leak of 8192 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
    #0 ... in malloc
    #1 ... in R_AllocStringBuffer src/main/memory.c:4969
    #2 ... in scanVector       src/main/scan.c:571
    #3 ... in do_scan          src/main/scan.c:1001
    #4 ... in bcEval_loop      src/main/eval.c:8150
    #5 ... in bcEval           src/main/eval.c:7533
    #6 ... in Rf_eval          src/main/eval.c:1167
    #7 ... in R_execClosure    src/main/eval.c:2398
    ...

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 8192 byte(s) leaked in 1 allocation(s).
```

## Suggested fix

`do_scan()` already installs an on-error cleanup for the same call: it
sets up a context whose `cend` handler, `scan_cleanup()`, releases the
connection and the `quoteset` buffer on a non-local exit:

```
begincontext(&cntxt, CTXT_CCODE, R_GlobalContext->call, R_BaseEnv,
             R_BaseEnv, R_NilValue, R_NilValue);
cntxt.cend = &scan_cleanup;
cntxt.cenddata = &data;
```

The cleanest fix is to bring the string buffer under that same cleanup.
For example, add an `R_StringBuffer *buf` field to `LocalData`, point it
at the local buffer at the top of `scanVector()`/`scanFrame()`
(`d->buf = &strBuf;`), and free it in `scan_cleanup()`:

```
static void scan_cleanup(void *data)
{
    LocalData *ld = data;
    if (ld->buf) { R_FreeStringBuffer(ld->buf); ld->buf = NULL; }
    if (ld->con && !ld->ttyflag && !ld->wasopen) { ... }
    if (ld->quoteset && ld->quoteset[0]) { ... }
}
```

`R_FreeStringBuffer()` clears `buf->data`, so the existing normal-path
`R_FreeStringBuffer()` calls in `scanVector()`/`scanFrame()` become no-ops
after cleanup and there is no double free.

## How it was found

libFuzzer + AddressSanitizer harness driving `scan(text = <fuzz>, ...)`
with `what` set to `""`, `0`, and separators `,`/`\t`, embedding R via
`Rf_initEmbeddedR()`. The leak fires on essentially every input that
isn't a clean parse, so it surfaces immediately.

Created attachment 3774
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3774&action=edit>
Handle %w of '0' consistently in LC_CTYPE=C

r63319 introduced a boundary check for `w_strptime_internal` that was not
mirrored in `strptime_internal`, so we get this difference in behavior:

```
LC_CTYPE=C          Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
# [1] NA
LC_CTYPE=en_US.utf8 Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
# [1] "2026-01-04 UTC"
```

<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19125>

            Bug ID: 19125
           Summary: Integer arithmetic means '%z' for minute-level offsets
                    is incorrect
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: All
                OS: All
            Status: NEW
          Severity: minor
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:michaelchirico4@gmail.com|michaelchirico4@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3775
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3775&action=edit>
Express tz offset in seconds and thereby avoid truncation error

```
strptime("2020-01-01 -0001", "%Y-%m-%d %z", tz = "UTC")
# [1] "2020-01-01 00:00:36 UTC"
```

The problem is the `/30` is truncated to integer. We can overcome this by
moving the `*3600/100` step earlier and avoiding `/` as much as possible.

In fact, I think it's much more natural to express this calculation in the
units of seconds, as in the patch, but I may be missing a subtlety.

*[Bug 19126] New: Compilation fails with gcc -Werror=format-security*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19126>

            Bug ID: 19126
           Summary: Compilation fails with gcc -Werror=format-security
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: major
          Priority: P5
         Component: Installation
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:csardi.gabor@gmail.com|csardi.gabor@gmail.com>

Seems like after 90348 compilation fails on setups where
-Werror=format-security is set. E.g. this is Fedora 44 and gcc 16.1.1:

```
fedora-gcc16-1  | gcc -I../../src/extra -I../../src/extra/xdr -I.
-I../../src/include -I../../src/include  -I/usr/local/include -I../../src/nmath
-DHAVE_CONFIG_H   -fopenmp -fpic  -g -O2 -Wall -pedantic -mtune=native
-Werror=format-security -Wp,-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 -fexceptions
-fstack-protector-strong -fstack-clash-protection -fcf-protection
-Werror=implicit-function-declaration -Wstrict-prototypes  -c array.c -o
array.o
fedora-gcc16-1  | array.c: In function 'dim2total':
fedora-gcc16-1  | array.c:302:9: error: format not a string literal and no
format arguments [-Werror=format-security]
fedora-gcc16-1  |   302 |         error(ErrMsg);
fedora-gcc16-1  |       |         ^~~~~
fedora-gcc16-1  | cc1: some warnings being treated as errors
```
<https://github.com/r-hub/containers/actions/runs/30978440969/job/92217515789>

Another example is Fedora 42 and gcc 15.2.1:
<https://github.com/r-hub/containers/actions/runs/30978440969/job/92217515853>

Fix:
```
error("%s", ErrMsg);
```

This is currently not a security issue per se because `ErrMsg` is always a
(translated) literal.
